summary: Frontend-only test of new column-resize feature on /customer-invoice-overview. Verified drag-to-resize on Customer, month, and Δ columns; header-sort not toggled by drag; data-resizing toggles true/false; min-width clamp works (m2 clamped to 84); persistence via localStorage 'cio-col-widths-v1' verified after reload; Reset column widths link appears/disappears and restores 30% share for Customer; header sort click still toggles asc/desc; horizontal scroll works at 1366×768 when widths overflow container; no console errors. One minor hit-test bug found on the Δ column resize handle.

ui_bugs.issue: The resize handle for the Δ column has only ~4px of hittable area instead of 8px. The handle span uses `-mr-1` (margin-right:-4px) so it extends 4px past its parent <th>. For inner columns this is fine, but for the last (delta) column that 4px overshoot lies outside the table wrapper (overflow-x:auto clips it). elementFromPoint at the visual center (x=1888) returns <main>, not the handle. Only x=1884-1887 fires mousedown → users who click on/near the visible right edge miss and don't get a resize. Verified: mousedown at handle.boundingBox center → data-resizing stays false, width unchanged, localStorage not written. Mousedown at (handleX+1) → resize works normally and Δ width grows from 160→240 after +80px drag.

action_items: Fix Δ-column resize handle hit area: for the last column, remove the `-mr-1` overshoot (or apply `-ml-1` instead) so the entire 8px handle stays inside the table wrapper's clip region. Alternatively, widen the handle to w-3 and keep it flush with the th right edge.
critical_code_review_comments: ResizeHandle uses `absolute right-0 -mr-1 w-2` — the -4px overshoot is clipped by the ancestor overflow-x:auto for the last column, halving its hit target. Consider making the handle side-aware or padding the wrapper by 4px right.

startResize's setWidths((w) => ({ ...w, [col]: ... })) inside stop() reads state at closure time; safe here because move() also updates via functional form, but if widths is null on first drag (before useEffect fills defaults), spreading null gives {} and only the dragged column is persisted. Consider guarding startResize when widths is null.

The `Reset column widths` link visibility check depends on `localStorage.getItem(WIDTH_KEY)` which is read on every render — fine, but this couples render to localStorage; would be cleaner to derive from a `hasCustomWidths` state.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Feature works end-to-end. Only remaining issue is hit-target width on the LAST column's resize handle (Δ) — the -mr-1 overshoot is clipped by wrapper overflow. Reproduce: on 1920 viewport, get boundingBox of [data-testid=cio-resize-delta] (x≈1884, w=8), call elementFromPoint(handleCenterX,y) → returns MAIN, not the handle span. Fix and re-verify by dragging at the handle's true center.
rca of the issue: ResizeHandle span has classes `absolute inset-y-0 right-0 w-2 -mr-1`. The -mr-1 margin-right:-4px shifts the visible/hit area 4px past the parent <th>'s right edge. For non-terminal columns this overlays harmlessly on the neighbor th. For the terminal Δ column, the 4px overshoot lies past the table's right edge, which is inside a wrapper with overflow-x:auto. That overflow clips the overshoot from hit-testing, so only the inner 4px of the 8px handle receives pointer events. Users clicking on the visible right edge of Δ miss the handle. Mitigation: drop `-mr-1` for the last column (or apply `-ml-1` there) so the full 8px sits inside the th.
